idiomatic: folio 4352

literal: Recorded in Guoyu; that sentence is absent—probably struck as unintelligible, which shows the corruption and lacuna are old.
idiomatic: Guoyu preserves the passage but not this line; it was likely dropped because it could not be parsed, so the damage is longstanding.

literal: "Although jiao compared with a duke, yet enjoying the benefit of a fief was still not pleasant": in the Northern edition, Palace edition, and Beishi juan 15, "jiao" (compare) is written "bo" (refute).
idiomatic: The clause "though matched against a duke's standing, the profit of a fief still brought no satisfaction" reads "compare" (jiao) as "refute" (bo) in the Northern and Palace editions and in Beishi juan 15.

literal: Comment: The general sense is that although demoted in rank to duke and still enjoying the profits of a fief, Yuan Pi nevertheless remained discontented.
idiomatic: Note: The point is that even after reduction to duke and retention of fief income, Yuan Pi was still unhappy.

literal: But whether written "jiao" or "bo," neither is easy to construe; there must be corruption and lacuna.
idiomatic: Neither reading makes good sense; the line is corrupt or incomplete.

literal: "Having zhang sentiment": in all editions a doubtful mark is entered below "qing" (sentiment).
idiomatic: The phrase "zhang sentiment" carries an editorial "?" after "qing" in every witness.

literal: Comment: "Zhang" is the same as "zhang" (rely on); "zhang sentiment" means the feeling of reliance—nothing doubtful.
idiomatic: Note: "Zhang" equals "rely upon"; "zhang sentiment" means dependence—no emendation is needed.

literal: Now deleted.
idiomatic: The doubtful mark is removed.

literal: "How could one bow with the multitude of officials to avoid the Central Commander": Cefu juan 271
idiomatic: "How could one stoop like the other officials to dodge the Central Commander": Cefu juan 271
folio 3214

literal: , Tongdian juan 24, entry on the Censor Central Commander, has the character "qu" (hasten) above "bi" (avoid).
idiomatic: ; Tongdian juan 24 (Censor Central Commander) inserts "hasten" (qu) before "avoid" (bi).

literal: Comment: By the syntax of the period, that character should be present; it is a lacuna.
idiomatic: Note: Contemporary usage requires the word; it dropped from the text.

literal: Niansheng sent his younger brother Tiansheng to garrison Longkou: in all editions and Beishi juan 15, "Long" (Long region) is written "Dragon" (long).
idiomatic: Niansheng dispatched his brother Tiansheng to hold Longkou; every edition and Beishi juan 15 write the place name "Long" as "Dragon."

literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 150
idiomatic: See Zizhi tongjian, juan 150
folio 4683

literal: states that Yuan Zhi and Tiansheng "fought at Longkou."
idiomatic: has Yuan Zhi and Tiansheng "battle at Longkou."

literal: Hu Zhu's note: "Longkou is the mouth of the Long dike."
idiomatic: Hu Sanxing glosses Longkou as the pass at the Long plateau.

literal: Comment: Juan 10 Annals of Emperor Suzong, eighth month of Zhenguang year 5; juan 59 Biography of Xiao Baoyin; and juan 73 Biography of Cui Yanbo all say Moqi Tiansheng routed Yuan Zhi east of Long.
idiomatic: Note: Suzong's annals (juan 10, Zhenguang 5.8), Xiao Baoyin's biography (juan 59), and Cui Yanbo's biography (juan 73) all place Moqi Tiansheng's great defeat of Yuan Zhi in Longdong.

literal: Writing "Long" is correct; now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: "Long" is the right graph; the text is corrected on that authority.

literal: Later the Tujing Hu and Lishi Hu, Chuyibing and others, rebelled: juan 28 Biography of Liu Ji writes "Chuyijuan" for "Chuyibing"; "juan" is probably correct.
idiomatic: Afterward the Tujing and Lishi Hu, with Chuyijuan and others, rose in revolt; Liu Ji's biography (juan 28) reads "Chuyijuan" where this annal has "Chuyibing"—"juan" is likely the true form.
